key_insight: In Sr2FeRuO6, B-site antisite disorder stabilizes a Griffiths-like magnetic phase and strongly localized charge transport, linking quenched disorder to both spin and conduction inhomogeneity.
engineering_relevance: The result highlights disorder engineering as a lever for tuning magnetic and transport behavior in hybrid double perovskites for spintronic and oxide-electronics applications.
method: Monoclinic structural analysis with significant B-site antisite disorder
Magnetic measurements to detect Griffiths-phase behavior and short-range ferromagnetic clusters
Electrical transport analysis across temperature regimes to identify polaronic and hopping conduction
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a robust Griffiths phase above the ordering temperature and a transport crossover from small-polaron hopping at high temperature to variable-range hopping at intermediate temperature.
watch_item: The strong disorder and localized transport may limit long-range functional performance and make device behavior sensitive to synthesis quality and defect control.
paper_title: Disorder-Induced Griffiths like Phase and Charge Localization in Sr2FeRuO6
